output.brief: The slowdown is not mainly about Corvane or the new hires. It comes from the credit policy refresh on 1 May. Clause 6.3 now requires a full appraisal for property loans above $150k, where the old threshold was $500k. Those loans used to get quick desktop valuations. Full appraisals take about 8.6 days at the valuation firm, against about 1.2 for desktop. The firm's speed hasn't changed. Valuation time for property loans rose from about 1.7 to about 8 days. Unsecured loans are back to about 5.9 days. Document collection is the same at the branches with new hires as elsewhere. The policy change was never assessed for its effect on processing time. I'm quite confident (about 85–90%). One gap: withdrawals rose, but the evidence doesn't tell us how much of that comes from slower approvals and how much from the new 30-day auto-close rule. Next steps: don't withhold Corvane's payment, and don't put the new hires on improvement plans. Take the measured delay to the credit risk committee alongside the audit finding that justified the change. They can decide whether to keep the $150k threshold or move it. Add a by-stage timing view to the dashboard. Check the withdrawal closure codes before spending money on a fee rebate.
